title: Impact of polypharmacy and antibiotics on fecal microbiome composition and function (PoMiBi)
summary: Wir möchten mit Hilfe der PoMiBi-Studie herausfinden, welchen Einfluss verschiedene Medikamente auf das Mikrobiom im Darm haben, da sich zunehmend Hinweise finden, dass auch Medikamente, die keine Antibiotika sind, Auswirkungen auf das Mikrobiom haben. Die Erkenntnisse könnten dabei helfen zu verstehen, warum manche Menschen empfindlicher für Infektionen sind, oder warum die antiinfektive Therapie bei verschiedenen Menschen unterschiedlich wirkt.

interventions.name: The microbiome of patients over the age of 60 with polypharmacy (more than 5 non-antibiotic medications) with and in a control group without current antibiotic medication will be investigated.
As a further control arm, the microbiome of people aged 60 and over without polypharmacy will be examined.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- capable of giving consent or consent by patient representative additionally for subject group 1.:
- long-term use of 5 or more non-antibiotic medications (home medication) additionally for subject group 2:
- long-term use of 5 or more non-antibiotic medications (home medication) and current intake of at least one antibiotic
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute cancer
- Diagnosis of other diseases or conditions that are associated with changes in the intestinal microbiota, e.g. chronic inflammatory bowel disease, artificial bowel outlet (stoma), current diarrhea
- Use of antibiotics in the last 3 months before recruitment additionally for subject group 3:
- acute illness or inpatient treatment in hospital
- Permanent intake of more than 2 medications (home medication)
additionally for subject group 4:
- Permanent intake of more than 2 medications (home medication)
